findings.title: Fix `enableSqlExpressions`, which always returns false and ignores the feature flag
Update or skip existing tests that rely on the DuckDB-backed `TablesList` / `QueryFramesInto`
Remove dead query-building code and the misleading `duckDB` name in `TablesList`
SQL commands built outside `ReadQuery` bypass the new gate and fail with an opaque error
Make the disabled-feature error message clear and actionable

response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Fix `enableSqlExpressions`, which always returns false and ignores the feature flag

Affected:
- pkg/expr/reader.go:194-200

Explanation:
Both branches return `false`, so the feature-flag lookup has no effect. The variable `enabled` is also assigned the negation of the flag, which reads backwards and suggests the logic is wrong.

The function looks like a feature-flag gate but is really a hard-coded "off" switch. Two problems follow:
- A later maintainer could "fix" one branch and accidentally re-enable SQL expressions while the backend is still a stub.
- Linters (staticcheck/gocritic) may flag the identical branches.

If the intent is to disable SQL expressions unconditionally, make that explicit. If the intent is to gate on the flag, return the flag's value.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
// SQL expressions are temporarily disabled: the DuckDB backend was removed
// and pkg/expr/sql.DB is a stub. Re-enable by checking FlagSqlExpressions
// once a new engine is available.
func enableSqlExpressions(_ *ExpressionQueryReader) bool {
	return false
}
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Test
Title: Update or skip existing tests that rely on the DuckDB-backed `TablesList` / `QueryFramesInto`

Affected:
- pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:22-26
- pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12-22
- pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-100

Explanation:
`TablesList` now always fails, because `RunCommands` returns "not implemented". `SQLCommand.Execute` also always fails, because `QueryFramesInto` returns "not implemented".

Any existing tests that assert parsed table names or successful execution will now fail. Likely candidates are `pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go`, `pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go`, and reader tests for `QueryTypeSQL`. Those files are not visible in this diff, so verify them in the repo.

These tests need to be removed, skipped, or rewritten to assert the new "not implemented" behavior. Otherwise CI will break.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
func TestTablesList(t *testing.T) {
	t.Skip("SQL expressions disabled: DuckDB backend removed")
	// ...
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Remove dead query-building code and the misleading `duckDB` name in `TablesList`

Affected:
- pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:22-26

Explanation:
`TablesList` still escapes quotes and builds a DuckDB-specific `json_serialize_sql` command, then passes it to a stub that ignores it. The local variable is still named `duckDB` even though DuckDB is gone.

This dead code is misleading. It implies the SQL is still parsed by DuckDB.

Either short-circuit with an explicit error, or at least rename the variable and add a comment explaining the stub.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
func TablesList(rawSQL string) ([]string, error) {
	return nil, errors.New("sql expressions are not supported: no SQL engine available")
}
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Implementation
Title: SQL commands built outside `ReadQuery` bypass the new gate and fail with an opaque error

Affected:
- pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-103
- pkg/expr/reader.go:128-132

Explanation:
The "not implemented" gate exists only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. Other code paths may build an `SQLCommand` directly, for example the legacy node unmarshalling in `nodes.go` via `UnmarshalSQLCommand`. I can't verify those callers from this diff.

On such paths, users who have `FlagSqlExpressions` enabled would get a generic "not implemented" error from `sql.TablesList` or `db.QueryFramesInto`, with no hint that the feature is disabled. Execution would also log at Error level on every query.

Consider failing early in `UnmarshalSQLCommand` / `NewSQLCommand` with a clear, user-facing message, for example "SQL expressions are currently disabled".

Proposed fix:
~~~go
func NewSQLCommand(refID, rawSQL string) (*SQLCommand, error) {
	return nil, errutil.NotImplemented("sse.sqlExpressionsDisabled").
		Errorf("SQL expressions are currently disabled")
}
~~~

## 5) Severity: INFO | Type: Implementation
Title: Make the disabled-feature error message clear and actionable

Affected:
- pkg/expr/reader.go:129-132

Explanation:
"sqlExpressions is not implemented" is confusing for users who explicitly enabled the `sqlExpressions` feature flag. The feature *was* implemented and has now been disabled.

A clearer message, ideally a typed errutil error so the API returns a proper status instead of a 500, would reduce support confusion.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
if !enableSqlExpressions(h) {
	return eq, fmt.Errorf("SQL expressions are currently disabled")
}
~~~
